messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

NOTE: Communications in your area are sometimes subject to routine monitoring by the authorities.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: If you were looking for a textbook picture of a regime approaching collapse, this is close to what you'd expect.
ATMOSPHERE: Groups are forming openly, and the old caution about being seen together has largely dissolved.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] a veteran regime fixer known for quiet problem-solving has been sidelined without explanation
  - [Security Forces] This removes any serious doubt that past the point of concealment — an informant in the security services says internal surveillance has shifted from opposition to other security units
  - [Money And Logistics] This removes any serious doubt that barely perceptible — government payments are arriving on schedule, and contracts are being honored
  - [Street Mood] children in the street are chanting slogans they clearly learned from adults — the anger has permeated households
  - [Information Control] This removes any serious doubt that past the point of concealment — censorship is getting sloppier — critical posts survive longer before deletion
  - [Personal Observations] This removes any serious doubt that past the point of concealment — a colleague who never discusses politics asked you hypothetically what you'd do 'if things changed'
  - [Diplomatic Signals] diplomatic social events are proceeding with normal attendance — no embassies are in bunker mode (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Institutional Functioning] environmental inspections are being conducted on schedule — even the less glamorous parts of government are operational (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - If the regime has foreign backers who might intervene to prop it up at the last moment.
  - Whether the top is losing control, or intentionally tightening the circle and freezing everyone else out.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: "I think it's safe to say that the regime is on shaky ground - the signs are all pointing to a collapse, from the way people are openly gathering and speaking out, to the security forces turning on each other. I'm not sure what the trigger will be or when it will happen, but it feels like we're getting close to a tipping point."
